inflate

/in-FLAYT/ - rhymes with late · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Inflate means to increase something beyond its true or proper amount.

The two organizers each inflated their crowd counts until the two rallies, by their own arithmetic, outnumbered the city.

Example

The cottage listing said 'nearly 1,200 square feet.' The tape measure said 900 — the listing had inflated the number by counting the porch, the toolshed, and a crawlspace no adult could stand up in. Nothing was invented; a true figure had simply been pumped up until it read half again its size.

Inflate is the precise verb because the trick runs in one direction and works on amounts. The root means 'to blow into': the listing blew air into 900 until it looked like 1,200. Lying invents; inflating takes a real number, price, or claim and swells it past its proper size.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

exaggerate: Exaggerate stretches something real in the telling — the fish gets longer, the traffic worse, the crowd rowdier — and it works on anything a story can hold. Inflate does its stretching to amounts: a figure, a price, a total pumped past its true size, usually on paper.

pad: Pad means to bulk something out with filler that adds nothing real — extra pages in a report, invented hours on a timesheet. Inflate keeps the same dishonesty but swells the number itself instead of stuffing material in around it. Padding adds bulk; inflating feeds a figure air.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

understate: play a thing down below its true size

deflate: let the excess out — of a figure, a price, or an ego

Where it sits · how far from the truth it strays

overstate → inflate → falsify

overstate vs. inflate: Overstating stretches the truth a size or two; inflating pumps it well past its proper amount — the difference between 'a strong turnout' and doubling the count.

falsify vs. inflate: Falsify sits past inflate: an inflated figure at least began as a real one, while a falsified figure walks away from the truth altogether.

Which word fits?

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-: into

Root — flat-: to blow (Latin flare)

Suffix — -e: verb ending

Put it together: In- (into) + flat- (to blow — Latin flare) + -e = to blow into. What you blow into swells: a balloon, a price, a résumé. The balloon never left the word: an inflated claim is a balloon-shaped truth, bigger than its contents.

Use the root in a new word: deflate: One sharp question from the auditor deflated the sales projections by half.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, often accusing

Inflate is the verb of crooked arithmetic: figures, prices, titles, and claims pumped past their true amount, usually by someone with something to gain. Magnify, its unit-mate, distorts how big a thing appears without touching the books; amplify strengthens something real; intensify says the degree itself rose. When a number has been fed air, inflate is the accusation.
